title: Quantification of zinc intoxication of Candida glabrata after phagocytosis by primary macrophages
protocol: Pick one fungal colony with a sterile tip and inoculate into 5 mL liquid YPD medium in culture tubes.
Let the cells grow in the tube for 4–8 hours at 30°C with agitation at 200 rpm and an angle of 45°.
Dilute the fungal cell suspension 1:10 with fresh YPD to stay within the linear range of the spectrophotometer.
Measure the optical density at 600 nm (OD600) in a spectrophotometer to follow growth.
Adjust fungal cells to reach logarithmic growth phase (OD600 = 0.8–1) on the next day with the appropriate formula.
Let cells grow for an additional 14-17 hours at 30°C with agitation at 200 rpm and an angle of 45°.
It is highly discouraged to use fungal cell suspensions with OD600 above 2; in this case, set up new fungal cultures.
Set up YPD culture volume sufficient for the required number of C. glabrata cells the next day.
Include an un-inoculated tube filled with liquid YPD media when inoculating Candida.
Harvest differentiated BMDMs by gently scraping them off the culture dish into a 50 mL conical tube.
Pellet BMDMs at 300 × g for 6 min at room temperature.
Resuspend macrophages in 1 mL fresh macrophage medium.
Take an aliquot to count cells using a CASY cell counter.
Seed 2 × 10^5 macrophages/well into a 24-well plate in triplicates for each experimental condition.
Add macrophage medium at a final volume of 1 mL/well.
Let BMDMs equilibrate for 17 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Harvest Candida cells when OD600 = 1 is reached by transferring the fungal suspension into a 50 mL conical tube.
Take an aliquot to check for morphology of the fungal cells and possible contaminations under the microscope.
Pellet fungal cells at 3,000 × g for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in the same volume of PBS.
Repeat the centrifugation and remove supernatant.
Resuspend the fungal pellet in 1 mL PBS.
Take a small aliquot of 10 μL to determine cell count in a CASY cell counter.
Suspend fungal cells in macrophage medium at a final cell number of 4 × 10^6 counts/mL.
Heat-stress fungal cells by placing them on a thermomixer at 65°C for 1 minute.
Infect macrophages by adding 50 μL of Candida suspension/well (2 × 10^5 C. glabrata cells).
Incubate host-pathogen mixtures in the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Prepare a 10 μM Zinpyr-1 solution 15 minutes before the end of the infection and store at RT in the dark.
Aspirate culture medium after 2–12 hours of infection.
Gently wash each well 3 times with 1 mL PBS at room temperature.
Add 300 μL of the Zinpyr-1 solution per well and incubate cells for 30 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Decant supernatant and wash each well 3 times with 1 mL PBS at room temperature.
Put plate on ice and add 300 μL of the SDS solution per well to liberate phagosomal Candida cells; incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Pre-cool a tabletop centrifuge to 4°C before use.
Fill each well with ice-cold PBS to 1 mL and harvest C. glabrata via pipetting.
Transfer volume of each well into separate 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes vigorously, ensuring the entire bottom is included.
Pellet fungal cell suspension at 21,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Prepare a fresh PI solution (2 μg/mL).
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 200 μL of PI solution.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature in the dark.
Add 800 μL of ice-cold PBS to achieve a final volume of 1 mL.
Pellet at 21,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate supernatant and wash fungal pellet twice with 1 mL ice-cold PBS.
Resuspend fungal cell pellet after the last washing step in 300 μL of PBS.
